title: Flash NanoPrecipitation for the Encapsulation of Hydrophobic and Hydrophilic Compounds in Polymeric Nanoparticles
protocol: Prepare equipment for encapsulation process.
Procure and validate a CIJ (Coaxial Intertwiner Jet) mixer.
Clean all fittings on the CIJ mixer to ensure snugness and unobstructed outlet tubing.
Attach 5 mL luer lock syringes containing 2-3 mL of cleaning solvent to each inlet adapter of the CIJ mixer in a fume hood.
Depress the syringe plungers steadily over a few seconds to empty contents through the mixing chamber into a waste container.
Remove used syringes; these can be retained and reused for subsequent rounds of cleaning between FNP runs.
Dry the CIJ mixer internals using a nitrogen (N2) stream directed through a male luer adapter attached to the end of a N2 line.
Dissolve the hydrophobic compound in unstabilized THF at 10 mg/mL using a vortex mixer until dissolved.
If necessary, sonicate the mixture for 1-2 minutes to ensure complete dissolution.
Dissolve the block copolymer stabilizer in THF at 10 mg/ml at approximately the same volume as the hydrophobic compound solution.
Mix the polymer solution with a vortex mixer until dissolved.
Place the solution in a sonication bath for 1-2 min if necessary to aid solids dissolution.
Pipette 0.25 mL of the vitamin E solution into a 1.5 mL centrifuge tube.
Pipette 0.25 mL of the polymer solution into the same tube containing vitamin E.
Mix well on a vortex mixer for 5-10 s.
Centrifuge the tube at 1000 x g for 5-10 s optionally to recover any liquid stuck to the cap, improving reproducibility between CIJ runs.
Pipette 0.525 mL of deionized water into a second 1.5 mL centrifuge tube as the antisolvent stream.
Pipette 4 mL of deionized water into a 20 mL scintillation vial or other suitable container as a quench bath.
Place a small magnetic stir bar in the quench bath.
Position the open quench bath vial below the cleaned CIJ mixer on a stir plate in a fume hood.
Begin stirring the quench bath via the magnetic stir bar at around 75% max speed.
Draw the full volume from the antisolvent tube using a 1 mL polypropylene syringe fitted with a blunt-tip needle.
Carefully remove all air bubbles from the syringe and dispose of the blunt tip needle in a sharps container.
Prime the plunger so that the stream comes just to the syringe opening.
Attach the syringe to one of the CIJ inlet fittings.
Depress syringes rapidly, smoothly, and uniformly to collect effluent in the quench bath vial.
Set aside CIJ mixer with attached syringes.
Remove stir bar from vial containing NP dispersion.
Cap the vial securely after removing stir bar.
Hold CIJ mixer over a waste solution container and remove syringes.
Dispose of used syringes carefully.
Repeat cleaning step 1.1 before the next FNP trial.
Pipette 100 μL of NP dispersion into a plastic cuvette for DLS analysis.
Add 900 μL of quench bath solvent to the cuvette.
Mix well by pipetting up and down or by mild shaking.
Prepare solvent, antisolvent, and quench solutions in fume hood.
Complete cleaning and preparation procedures using DMSO as a cleaning solvent.
Complete a second rinse with THF.
Dissolve maltodextrin (MD) with dextrose equivalent (DE) of 4-7 and average molecular weight = 3,275 g/mol in DMSO at 10 mg/mL to complete the desired number of FNP runs.
Mix the maltodextrin solution with a vortex mixer until dissolved.
Place the solution in a sonication bath for 1-2 min if necessary to aid in solids dissolution.
Create a block copolymer stabilizer (i.e., poly(styrene)-b-poly(acrylic acid), PS5k-b-PAA4.8k) stock solution in THF at 11.1 mg/mL.
Ensure the polymer solution volume is approximately the same as in step 2.1.2.
Prepare the solvent stream input by combining 0.250 mL of the 3k MD solution, 0.225 mL of polymer solution, and 0.025 mL deionized water in a 1.5 mL centrifuge tube.
Mix well on a vortex mixer for 5-10 s.
Optionally, centrifuge the tube at 1000 x g for 5-10 s to recover any liquid stuck to the cap.
Prepare a crosslinker solution of calcium chloride (CaCl2) dihydrate in methanol at 25.0 mg/mL.
Prepare the antisolvent stream by pipetting 0.5 mL of chloroform into a microcentrifuge tube.
Add 0.05 mL of the crosslinker solution (totaling 0.55 mL) to the microcentrifuge tube.
Mix well on a vortex mixer for 5-10 seconds.
Optionally, centrifuge the tube at 1000 x g for 5-10 seconds to recover any liquid stuck to the cap.
Add 4 mL of chloroform to a 20 mL scintillation vial to form the quench bath.
Place a small magnetic stir bar in the vial.
To characterize NP size using DLS, pipette 100 μL of the NP dispersion into a glass cuvette.
Add 900 μL of the solvent used for the quench bath to the cuvette.
Mix well by pipetting up and down or by light agitation of the cuvette.
Prepare a 50 mg/mL solution of ovalbumin in deionized water.
Dilute 75 μL of the OVA solution with 0.675 mL of DMSO to generate a 5 mg/mL solution of OVA in DMSO containing 10% water by volume.
Mix well and centrifuge briefly as described previously.
Dissolve the block copolymer stabilizer in DMSO at 6 mg/mL.
Mix well and sonicate if needed.
Pipette 0.75 mL of the dissolved stabilizer into a 1.5 mL centrifuge tube.
Pipette 0.75 mL of THF into another 1.5 mL centrifuge tube.
Pipette 1.85 mL of chloroform into a glass scintillation vial.
Prepare a 60.0 mg/mL calcium chloride dihydrate crosslinker solution in methanol.
Mix using a vortex mixer.
Prepare a 4.17 mg/mL ammonia solution in methanol.
Add 5.25 mL of chloroform to a 15 mL centrifuge tube as the quench bath.
Place the O-ring into the groove.
Ensure the O-ring fits well and shows no signs of wear or damage.
Allow a worn O-ring to air dry overnight before use if necessary.
Dispose of an O-ring if its shape does not recover overnight.
Align the mixing disk holes with the pegs on the top disk.
Push the two pieces together, ensuring the O-ring is not displaced.
Loosen the outlet tubing fitting to allow complete tightening of the disk assembly.
Disassemble and apply a food- or pharmaceutical-grade anti-seize to the threading if it catches during assembly.
Manually tighten the assembly after applying anti-seize.
Fit the spanner wrench to the top disk pegs and snugly tighten the assembly.
Tighten the outlet tubing fitting so that it sits firmly against the bottom face of the mixing geometry.
Ensure that the syringe fittings on the top disk are snug.
Place the assembled mixer onto the mixer stand with the outlet tubing extending below the support plate.
Support the mobile plate so that it is suspended out of the way of the work space.
Optionally, lower the mobile plate so that it comes to rest on the mechanical stops.
Ensure alignment so that the plate also comes to rest immediately before contacting the empty syringes.
Optionally, loosen and reposition the mechanical stops if needed.
Remove the glass syringes and reset the mobile plate out of the way.
Place the open quench bath below the outlet tubing to collect the effluent.
Draw Solution A into a 1 mL gas-tight syringe using a blunt tip needle.
Remove all air bubbles from the solution in the syringe.
Dispose of the needle used for drawing the solution.
Prime the solution to the end of the syringe luer fitting.
Repeat this process for Solutions B and C.
Draw Solution D into a 2.5 mL gas-tight syringe using a blunt tip needle.
Remove all air bubbles from the solution in the syringe.
Dispose of the needle used for drawing the solution.
Prime the solution to the end of the syringe luer fitting.
Assemble the four syringes onto the mixer in alphabetical order.
Check that no syringe height is significantly different from others.
Grip the bearing housing on both sides of the mobile plate.
Slowly lower the mobile plate so it rests evenly but barely touching the syringes.
Steadily and smoothly depress the plate to complete the operation in about 0.5-1 s.
Remove and cap the quench bath tube containing the NP dispersion.
Hold the mixer with attached syringes over a waste container.
Remove the syringes, allowing hold-up volume to drain into the container.
Disassemble the mixer using the spanner wrench while holding it upside down.
Rinse the outlet tubing with several milliliters of solvent (e.g., acetone).
Dry the outlet tubing with air or nitrogen.
Rinse the mixing geometry with a good solvent (e.g., deionized water or DMSO).
Rinse the mixing geometry with acetone using several milliliters from a spray bottle.
Dry the mixing geometry with an air or nitrogen stream.
Rinse the O-ring in a stream of deionized water.
Blot dry the O-ring.
Rinse the top disk thoroughly with acetone until visually clean.
Dry the surface and syringe fittings with an air or nitrogen stream.
Rinse each syringe with several milliliters of deionized water or acetone from a solvent bottle.
Apply a final rinse of several milliliters of acetone to the syringes.
Air dry both the top disk and syringes before next use.
Add 50 μL of calcium chloride dihydrate crosslinker solution dropwise while stirring at about 75% maximum speed.
Add 50 μL of ammonia solution dropwise while stirring at 75% maximum speed.
Age for at least 30 min.
Characterize the NP size as described in steps 2.3.1 and 2.3.2.
Process the NP dispersion to produce either microparticles or coated NPs as described in the literature.
Prepare the solvent and antisolvent solutions at the desired composition and volume for scale-up formulation.
Clean and sterilize the mixer in place using a suitable protocol if required before NP formation.
Rinse sequentially with CIP 100, water to neutral pH, CIP 200, water to neutral pH, and a suitable solvent.
Attach sterile filters to the inlets of the mixer when necessary.
Load solutions into gas-tight syringes.
Attach PTFE tubing with luer adapter to syringes.
Prime solutions to end of tubing manually.
Load syringes into a syringe pump.
Attach syringes to mixer inlets on CIJ or MIVM as required.
Set volumetric flow rates to match manual operation (e.g., 30-60 mL/min per stream).
Simultaneously begin the pumps.
Collect about 5-10 mL of effluent as waste initially.
Begin collecting in the quench bath after initial waste collection.
